minutes.headline: Board member says school district left ~$600,000 of the override-funded FY25 budget unspent
minutes.summary: A Council on Aging meeting covering routine board business, minutes approval, a vote authorizing a member to keep working on a 41A senior tax exemption, financial and staffing updates for the senior center, and several new initiatives discussed informally (a proposed free/reduced building-permit process for seniors, a proposed "Mary Padulla Day," input to the town's master plan, and hospital-closure state aid). The most pointed moment was a board member's criticism that the school district finished FY25 with roughly $600,000 unspent despite a town override.

votes.motion: Approve Jack continuing to work on the 41A tax exemption on behalf of/relating to the Council on Aging

budget_items.topic: FY25 school budget surplus after override
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said the school committee's year-end closing showed a large amount of the FY25 override-funded budget went unspent, calling it something residents on both sides of the override should be upset about.

budget_items.topic: COA program budget FY26 to date
budget_items.what_was_said: The board was told spending is normal and early in the year, with only a fraction of the program budget used so far.

Money budgeted for a not-yet-filled full-time meal site manager position is currently being used for current kitchen staff; any leftover funds at year-end could potentially be transferred with select board approval.

The state has allocated money to be split among communities affected by a hospital closure in Ashoba/Ayer area, but the distribution formula and amounts per town are not yet known; the fire chief separately estimated an increased cost to Lunenburg from the closure.
The historical commission's replica cane was described as inexpensive, and a board member suggested letting the recipient keep it given the low cost.
A first quote for new senior-center-appropriate furniture came back far higher than expected; the center is seeking a second quote from the vendor the library used.

budget_items.topic: Proposed fee waiver for senior building permits
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member proposed waiving building permit fees for seniors on small jobs, estimating how many local permits and how much fee revenue this would involve, framing it as an outreach/education tool as much as a cost item.

transfers.description: Possible transfer of unused meal-site-manager salary funds at year end, pending select board approval

decisions.decision: Volunteer recognition will follow the town's National Volunteer Appreciation Week celebration already planned for a Monday in April rather than a separate fall event.
Board agreed the historical commission may participate going forward in Boston Post Cane presentations alongside the select board and senior center.
Center hours will revert to closing earlier (until 5) on weekdays other than Wednesday starting in November through February, keeping only Wednesday evenings open late.
Board agreed to tell the planning process that an assisted-living facility should be characterized as a 'must have,' not just 'nice to have,' for the town given the loss of medical facilities.
Board member will develop a short presentation on a proposed senior building-permit fee waiver to bring back to the board before seeking select board approval.
Board expressed general support for creating an annual 'Mary Padulla Day' honoring the town's late longtime town clerk and state senator, with details on date/format to be worked out.

what_happened.line: A board member said the district ended FY25 with a large share of its override-funded budget unspent, calling it something residents on both sides should question.
The board voted to authorize a member to keep working on a senior property tax exemption under state statute 41A.
A board member proposed waiving building permit fees for seniors on small jobs and will bring a presentation back to the board before seeking select board approval.
The board agreed to tell the town's master planning process that an assisted-living facility should be a "must have" given the area's loss of medical facilities.
Senior center hours will revert to an earlier weekday closing time from November through February, with only Wednesday evenings staying open late.

why_it_matters: The unspent-funds comment raises a question about how override money approved by voters for the schools was actually used in FY25 -- the school budget vs. actual spending is a separate accounting question this board did not itself resolve.

The 41A vote keeps alive a path toward property tax relief for qualifying seniors, and the proposed permit fee waiver would touch town permit revenue and senior services if it advances to the select board.
The push for assisted-living to count as a "must have" in the master plan, and the seasonal cut to senior center hours, both affect what services and facilities seniors in town can expect.

They differ on who was present, because our attendee list is incomplete and misheard, and on several details that exist in only one record (the fee-waiver decision, the percent figures, the Mary Padula Day wording).
